subject: Post-demo: concurrency, streaming & rate-cap clarification
messages:
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@finledger.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finledger.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: clarification on concurrency & streaming needs

Hi Evelyn / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo today — the team found the streaming demo and connection pooling details really helpful. Before we push this through procurement we need some concrete answers on a few production constraints so we can model SLOs internally:

- Latency target: we want p95 <= 300ms for single-turn interactive flows (avg payload ~512 tokens). Can Redwood confirm typical p95 for models in your catalog at that token length on hosted vs dedicated?
- Throughput: our first-phase target is ~120 req/s sustained, with headroom for short bursts. How do you handle short bursts (30–60s) and what burst windows do you enforce?
- Concurrency / connection pooling: our backend will open multiple parallel connections per worker. What are the per-API-key connection limits, and do you support HTTP/2 multiplexing (N streams per connection)?
- Streaming: ~70% of our calls will be streaming. Are there separate quotas or throttles for streaming vs non-streaming requests?

If you can send a quick summary and any docs/ratecards, that would help us finish the technical review.

Best,
Liam
Liam O'Neill
Senior Product Manager — FinLedger
liam.oneill@finledger.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finledger.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: clarification on concurrency & streaming needs

Hi Liam — great questions, appreciate the clear list. Quick recap + items attached.

Summary (high level):
- Latency: For models in our curated catalog, typical hosted p95 for ~512 tokens is 180–320ms depending on model family and region. Dedicated capacity provides tighter p95 (often sub-250ms) because you get reserved GPU pools and predictable kernel placement. We can share specific per-model perf profiles once you tell us which model variant you want to lock.

- Throughput & bursts: Our hosted tier enforces per-key sustained QPS and short burst windows. Typical default: sustained quota 200 QPS with a 5x burst multiplier for 30s for eligible accounts. We negotiate higher sustained limits for pilots and Dedicated contracts.

- Connections & multiplexing: We support HTTP/2 with stream multiplexing. Default practical guidance: design for 4 concurrent request streams per long-lived connection; HTTP/2 can carry ~10 simultaneous streams but we recommend grouping callers with a connection pool (client-side) to avoid head-of-line queuing. For Dedicated customers we can raise concurrent stream guidance and tune server-side concurrency.

- Streaming: Streaming calls count toward QPS and concurrent-stream quotas but do not have a separate throttle. Long-lived streams hold concurrency slots for their lifetime — worth factoring in for high-percent streaming workloads.

Next steps: I attached a simple connection topology diagram and our current ratecard (v2).
[Attachment: finledger-conn-diagram.pdf (application/pdf, 284KB)]
[Attachment: redwood-ratecard-v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 56KB)]

If you can send the expected peak concurrent workers and an estimate of streams-per-worker, I can propose two options:
1) Hosted pilot (30–90 days) with a temporary quota bump and a canary rollout at 100 QPS, monitoring tokens and latency; or
2) Dedicated capacity quote that guarantees higher sustained QPS and higher per-key concurrency.

Evelyn — I know procurement timeline is tight. Happy to jump on a call and walk Priya through the proposed numbers.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Principal SE — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: concurrency, streaming & rate-cap clarification

Thanks Liam — and thanks Ben for the clear summary and the attachments. To get procurement moving and to produce a concrete pilot proposal, we need three signal numbers from your side by EOD Tuesday:

1) Expected peak concurrent client sessions (users actively interacting at the same time). Example: 300 concurrent interactive users.
2) Typical backend worker count and parallelism: number of workers that will fan out calls and how many parallel requests per worker (e.g., 20 workers * 6 parallel = 120 parallel requests).
3) Streaming ratio and average session duration: % streaming vs non-streaming and median stream length (in seconds / tokens).

Once we have those, Ben will map to:
- recommended per-connection pool sizes and HTTP/2 multiplexing guidance,
- recommended trial quota bump (how much sustained QPS and burst we can grant during the pilot), and
- a concise SLA note if you prefer a Dedicated quote instead.

Operational asks: please confirm the procurement decision date so we can align SOW/DocuSign cadence. I put a couple links below for convenience.

HubSpot deal: https://redwood.hubspot.com/deal/1187
Draft SOW (DocuSign placeholder): https://www.docusign.com/placeholder/sow-finledger
Design folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3Cfinledger-integration

If it helps, we can do a 30-minute follow-up Wednesday 11:00–11:30 PT to lock numbers.

— Evelyn

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finledger.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: concurrency, streaming & rate-cap clarification

Thanks — quick answers below so you can size the pilot and generate numbers for procurement:

- Peak interactive users (concurrent): ~300 active users during trading hours (this is the worst 5% window).
- Backend fanout: 20 backend workers that will fan out requests; each worker may initiate up to 10 parallel API requests during peak processing (= 200 parallel requests).
- Streaming: ~70% of calls are streaming (live trade updates). Median stream length ~12s (~150 tokens).
- Expected steady throughput for pilot: 100–150 QPS; peak burst capacity needed: up to 700 QPS for 45–60s during heavy market events.

Procurement timeline: we have an internal decision target by Friday 2027-04-23. Procurement will want a written note on recommended per-key sustained QPS, burst windows, and whether a Dedicated commitment is necessary to meet p95 targets. Also please include an estimated cost delta for raising sustained quotas in hosted vs Dedicated.

Let us know if you need any more telemetry; happy to share a short synthetic load profile.

— Priya
Priya Shah
Head of Integrations — FinLedger
priya.shah@finledger.com
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finledger.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: concurrency, streaming & rate-cap clarification

Hi Priya — welcome, and thanks for the numbers. Quick operational proposal from CS so we can scope a safe pilot:

Pilot plan (recommended):
- Duration: 2 weeks internal pilot + 4-week canary for production readiness.
- Pilot quota: provision 150 QPS sustained with a temporary burst allowance to 700 QPS for 60s during scheduled load tests.
- Canary rollout: start with 100 QPS to a single region, monitor p95 latency and token cost for 48h, then step to full pilot traffic.
- Telemetry: we'll share a lightweight telemetry dashboard and a Slack hook for p95/err/error-rate alerts.
- Connection guidance: recommend client pool sizing = 8 persistent HTTP/2 connections with up to 10 streams each for your worker cluster (gives safety headroom vs 10 streams/conn). Ben will validate in his sizing doc.

Next steps: Ben + I will prepare a short pilot SOW and a scoped cost delta for Hosted vs Dedicated. Evelyn — can you push the DocuSign SOW draft to procurement when ready? Priya — I'll schedule a kickoff after you confirm Friday as the decision date.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
